subject: Zephyr renewal: utilization gating and staged GPU onboarding
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@zephyrhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01 09:12 -0700
Subject: Zephyr renewal: utilization gating and staged GPU onboarding

Hi Maria —

Thanks again for a constructive call yesterday. Per our discussion, I wanted to put a concise proposal in writing so your procurement and engineering teams can review:

Summary proposal
- Base renewal: keep current Dedicated tranche (8xA100 equiv) for the next 12 months.
- Staged onboarding: add 4 GPUs immediately upon renewal signing (2-week lead), with conditional automatic addition of +8 GPUs when sustained utilization exceeds 65% across peak windows for 7 consecutive days.
- Hysteresis / gating: 65% sustained avg + spike tolerance (up to 80% for single-day peaks) to avoid oscillation.
- Credits: we can offer a one-time onboarding credit of $15k toward your first month on the additional 4 GPUs.

Why this structure
- You told us that Q3 experiments will likely double peak inference throughput; staged onboarding prevents over-commit while giving runway for burst events.
- The utilization gating prevents frequent scaling churn and keeps latency SLOs predictable.

Attachments: Ben attached a forecast model and a GPU mapping + latency matrix that show the math and how latency changes by GPU mix.

Ask / next steps
1) Can procurement confirm timelines for signing? (Procurement contact in cc).
2) Engineering: if you can share typical 95th pct seq lengths during peak windows, Ben will finalize the mapping.
3) If acceptable, I’ll draft an amendment to the renewal (addendum) that captures the staged tranche and trigger conditions.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the attachment.

— Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Thanks Ava — this looks promising. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we pull procurement into a formal review: 

1) Can you confirm how "sustained utilization" is measured? Is it 1-min avg across the tranche or 5-min? We need to reconcile with our internal monitoring.
2) If we hit the 65% gate and the +8 GPUs auto-provision, what is the expected lead time for the additional capacity and will there be any change to per-token pricing during the scale event?

Procurement (cc): we’ll need estimated monthly spend on the immediate +4 GPUs and a clear statement on credits and invoicing cadence.

Also looping in James (ops) — James, can you share the 95th pct seq length (last 30 days) if you have it?

Best,
Maria
Head of AI Platform | Zephyr Health
ma.ria.gonzalez@zephyrhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02 13:24 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zephyr renewal: utilization gating and staged GPU onboarding

Hi Maria — quick answers (technical):

- Measurement: our gating uses a 5-minute rolling avg per GPU across the tranche aggregated to a weighted utilization (tokens/sec normalized by model FLOPs). For your setup that maps roughly to the same metric your Prometheus exporter reports as "gpu_util_5m".
- Lead time: immediate +4 GPUs are allocated from our available pool within 72 hours after contract effective date; the conditional +8 GPUs are reserved capacity we bring online within 7 days of trigger. We always keep a buffer for customers with signed staging agreements.
- Pricing: per-token and per-GPU unit pricing stays the same for the quarter of the renewal; any additional long-term commit would be negotiated separately. The onboarding credit Ava referenced is applied as a one-time invoice credit.

Attached is the forecast model with a couple of sensitivity tabs:
- Tab A (baseline): current traffic -> latency @ 99th pct
- Tab B (Q3 ramp): 2x peak -> shows when the 65% gating would fire
- Tab C (sustained spike): 7-day sustain math used for the gating logic

Excerpt from the forecast (summary):
- Current steady state: 8 GPUs show avg util ~48% with 95th token latency 180ms.
- Q3 projected peak (50% probability): sustained util ~68% -> trigger would add +8 GPUs, dropping 95th token latency to ~95ms.

If you want, I can switch the trigger from 65% to 70% if Zephyr prefers a higher threshold (tradeoff: later addition -> higher short-term latency risk).

— Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment stubs: zephyr_forecast_model_v2.xlsx, gpu-mapping-and-latency-matrix.pdf
